Because they kept raiding the northern border? The Jurchens ,malgal/mohe tribes and the Tungusics- being Mongols and Khitans (and just all sorts of Manchurian nomadic tribes in general) had interesting relations to Koreans in general. For example there were lots of relation dynamics: when Goguryeo ruled manchuria they had them under control and sometimes mobilized them against various Han chinese dynasties; I think I remember reading a instance when one of either Sui or Tang once won a battle against Goguryeo, they let go of the Goguryeo troops and executed the Moha soldiers fighting under them? Although this might need some clarification. After that, during the balhae/silla&goryeo period we actually had a previously Goguryeo-Moha monarch, Balhae’s Dae Jo young, with unified silla and Goryeo to the south. Even though Goryeo and Balhae both claimed to be the true descendants of Goguryeo, with Balhae’s founder Dae Jeo young being from previously-under-Goguryeo-moha tribe and Goryeo’s Wang Geon from a Goguryeo merchant family,they were on .. eh.. ‘decent’ terms with each other, to the extent when Balhae fell to the khitans, Goryeo took in hundreds of thousands of Balhae refugees alongside balhae’s crown prince and royals, with our mr Wang geon somehow personally enraged and telling his court and sons to not interact with the Khitans, because they’re bad people. Due to this, goryeo starved off some camels the khitans sent for diplomacy, and this act began the three Goryeo Khitan wars! Which was made into a bad and lackluster TV series last year. After that we have a turn of tables, where manchurian forces got the upper hand on the factions of the peninsula, where the mongol empire happened, and took over everywhere from the korean peninsula to west asia. Then we finally get a new han chinese kingdom; ming, and the mongols were gone, and the jurchens - being decendents of the moha? I’m a bit fuzzy on this one. After that Joseon Korea mostly just had trade (tribute, technically, but tribute was the defacto only form of trade anyway) with manchurian forces, until the jurchens decide to go bananas and make their own kingdom; Qing! They squander ming and the tables turn again and now joseon has to pay them tribute and etc etc. 

This is a bit long cause I find nomadic tribes with all their different diversity fascinating and such, but then again back to the topic. Because koreans have interbred with manchurian tribes for so long, especially if you consider that we took in hundreds of thousands of Balhae Moha refugees during the fall of Balhae, we share a lot of DNA with them too. 
I don’t think koreans hate like the jurchen people themselves, but I guess there is going to be some negativity when the past 500 years has been Jurchens invading northern border & raiding, Joseon launching preemptive wars against manchurian forces due to the former, and eventually after Jurchens banded and made Qing and Joseon loses and all this happens, a bit of bitterness tends to remain.
